claims.text: The uncoated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response under magnetic and pressure fields.
The uncoated alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and is susceptible to crack initiation and propagation.
A NiTi coating approximately 2 μm thick can be deposited by magnetron sputtering below 300°C and annealed at 350°C for 1 hour.
An optimized interlayer or surface pre-cleaning treatment will produce robust adhesion between the NiTi coating and the HEA substrate.
The specified deposition and annealing treatment can avoid altering the core alloy's phase structure.
The coated alloy will remain operational at magnetic fields of 0.8–1 T.
The coated alloy will remain operational at pressure fields up to 0.5 GPa.
The coated alloy will remain operational over 250–350 K.
The NiTi coating forms a ductile, energy-absorbing surface layer that buffers surface stresses.
Buffering surface stresses with the NiTi layer mitigates crack initiation and propagation.
An optimized bonded interface prevents delamination under operational loading.
The NiTi layer has inherent superelastic behavior under the stated operating conditions.
Superelastic deformation of the NiTi layer absorbs and redistributes applied mechanical stresses.
The NiTi coating and interface will not mechanically or thermodynamically interfere with the bulk caloric phase transformation.
The coating will increase the critical load for crack initiation by approximately 30–40% relative to the uncoated alloy.
The coating will keep the caloric transition-temperature shift within ±5% of the uncoated baseline during magnetic and pressure cycling.
The coating will keep the entropy-change deviation within ±5% of the uncoated baseline during magnetic and pressure cycling.
Long-term interface stability under combined mechanical and caloric cycling is uncertain.
